newsitem.title: UK: Fedex watching fuel surcharge very carefully.
newsitem.headline: Fedex watching fuel surcharge very carefully.

text.p: Federal Express Corp "is watching the cargo fuel surcharge situation very, very carefully but no immediate action is planned," a company spokesman told Reuters.

He was replying to a query as to whether Fedex planned to follow a number of major airlines -- mainly European -- in introducing a cargo fuel surcharge in November due to the sharp rise in jet fuel prices in recent months.

Fedex is the worldest largest scheduled freight carrier according to the latest International Air Transport Association (IATA) report, followed by Deutsche Lufthansa, Korean Airlines Ltd and Northwest Airlines.
"We want to continue to have the ability to provide our customers with the same service as before," the spokesman said.

Since last Friday, Lufthansa Cargo, KLM Royal Dutch Airlines NV, Air France, British Airways and Virgin Atlantic have all announced a cargo fuel surcharge. Swissair has set a cargo rate increase rather than a surcharge.
On October 30, Air France Cargo said its fuel costs rose by 40 percent between June and October this year.

The surcharges are averaging around US10 cents a kg or its equivalent in local currency to most destinations, although on domestic and some shorter flights, this may be slightly lower, industry sources noted.
They will take effect on dates ranging from November 1 to November 15

Airlines operating out of Hong Kong to Europe are introducing a surcharge of HK80 cents a kg from November 4 Monday and this is expected to be followed by a similar rise for trans-Pacific traffic, the chief executive officer of cargo airline, Air Hong Kong, Stanley Hui told Reuters.

IATA said this week it is holding an emergency meeting on November 13 in Geneva to review the impact of higher fuel costs on both passenger and cargo traffic. --Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax +44 171 542 5017
